scope: CVG-003 bounded clinical integrity of signed-prescription execution and administration-event persistence

criteria.description: Execution creation resolves an account-scoped active signed prescription and rejects missing, archived, unsigned, cross-account, cross-patient and cross-encounter sources before persistence.
criteria.limitations: The source and service proof is repository-local; prescribing authority, licensing and dose-safety decision support are outside this slice.

criteria.description: Medication, dosage, route and frequency are checked against the signed prescription and persisted from the canonical source rather than caller substitutions.
criteria.limitations: The durable parser follows the current clinical-entry prescription format; changes to signing/content semantics require revalidation.

criteria.description: Execute, suspend and resume use an observed or explicitly supplied positive expectedVersion and stale concurrent transitions fail with a stable conflict without a lost update.
criteria.limitations: Concurrency evidence is disposable local PostgreSQL and in-memory equivalent proof; target replica and connection-pool behavior remain open.

criteria.description: Execution and administration-event creation/update are compound repository operations in one tenant transaction; event failure rolls back execution state, with an equivalent in-memory mutex and rollback test.
criteria.limitations: The PostgreSQL transaction is verified in a disposable local database; crash/restart and production worker recovery are separate open gates.

criteria.description: HTTP action paths match exactly, validate UUID/prefixed identifiers/date-times and expectedVersion, require the manage permission before idempotency replay, and refresh execution/audit caches after commit or rollback.
criteria.limitations: The replay and route proof is local compiled HTTP semantics; deployed gateway, target authentication and network policy remain outside this gate.

criteria.description: The canonical migration preserves the tenant-local clinical source through a composite FK, and PostgreSQL integration verifies RLS/FORCE RLS plus non-disclosure under a restricted role.
criteria.limitations: Migration and role evidence is disposable local PostgreSQL; target ownership/grants and target RLS rollout are not certified.

criteria.description: Focused, package, API, database and workspace regressions, builds and security/static rails are green without weakening the global quality threshold.
criteria.limitations: Official aggregate coverage is 80.51% statements/lines, 80.22% branches and 87.70% functions, but the global configuration excludes the primary files of this slice; changed-code coverage is not inferred from the aggregate.

criteria.description: An independent read-only reviewer inspected the corrected implementation and current evidence and found no technical Critical or High finding; the prior governance-only condition is reconciled in the control plane.
criteria.limitations: This is a bounded local review and does not approve production, target, providers, parity, operations or release.

criteria.description: The bounded result is reconciled without promoting CVG-003, Vetus parity, clinical parity, enterprise readiness or release acceptance.
criteria.limitations: General Vetus parity remains 98/100 with 4/11 verified, clinical parity 100/100 with 2/3 verified, and enterprise readiness 95/100 with 42 PASS, 3 WARN and 1 FAIL.

gaps: This gate does not certify the full clinical journey, dose-safety decision support or professional licensing.

Target PostgreSQL ownership/grants/RLS, providers and homologation, backup/restore/RTO-RPO, distributed worker crash/recovery, remote CI, accessibility, operational LGPD, remaining Vetus parity and release acceptance remain open.
Aggregate coverage is not changed-code coverage because the global configuration excludes the principal files in this bounded slice.
conditions: Apply migration 0153 through the canonical migration rail before relying on the composite clinical-source FK in an existing installation.
Keep execution creation bound to a signed active prescription and preserve the compound repository boundary; any new writer requires revalidation.
Keep the parent CVG-003 and global ERP program IN_PROGRESS/PARTIAL and do not infer production or release approval from this local gate.

authority.actor: Ricardo (repository owner), via the original consolidation brief
authority.decision: Authorize reversible repository implementation, focused API tests and disposable PostgreSQL verification of signed-prescription linkage, optimistic concurrency and atomic execution/event persistence; exclude target, providers, credentials, production, deployment, external mutation and release acceptance.
authority.expires_or_revalidates: Revalidate before expanding beyond this execution/event boundary.

next_action: Keep CVG-003 and the global program IN_PROGRESS/PARTIAL; select the next gap only through fresh authority and preserve all external and release gates.
revalidation_triggers: New prescription, execution or administration-event writer
Changes to clinical-entry signing/archive semantics, tenant UoW, hydration or authorization
Changes to canonical migrations, target, providers, credentials, deployment or release scope
